entries.passageText: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
entries.reflection: Jesus calls loving God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength the first commandment. Love that holds nothing back is wholehearted.
studyPrompts: Which part of you holds back from God?
What would wholehearted love look like today?
Where do you give yourself fully?

entries.passageText: There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God. For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.
entries.reflection: Hebrews says there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God. Restlessness is not the end of the story. There is rest to enter.
studyPrompts: What makes you restless?
What would entering rest look like?
How could you keep a Sabbath, even briefly?

entries.passageText: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
entries.reflection: The psalmist cries from the ends of the earth when his heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I. When you are overwhelmed, look for higher ground and reach out for help.
studyPrompts: What is overwhelming you?
What is your rock?
Who could help you get to higher ground?

entries.passageText: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men, for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.
entries.reflection: Paul urges prayers for all people, including those in authority, so that we may live peaceful and quiet lives. Prayer for leaders is part of faith, whatever we think of them.
studyPrompts: Who is in authority over you?
How could you pray for them?
What does it mean to pray for leaders you disagree with?

entries.passageText: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
entries.reflection: Jesus told his disciples, come away to a quiet place and rest a while, because they had no time even to eat. Rest is something Jesus gives and commands.
studyPrompts: When did you last truly rest?
What keeps you from leisure?
Where could you rest a while this week?

entries.passageText: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.
entries.reflection: Paul urges us to present our bodies as a living sacrifice, which is our spiritual service. Sacrifice is a whole life offered, not one moment.
studyPrompts: What would offering your life as a living sacrifice look like?
What are you holding back?
How is your daily service an offering?

entries.passageText: Therefore we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.
entries.reflection: Hebrews says we must pay closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away. Drift happens slowly. Attention keeps us anchored.
studyPrompts: Where have you drifted?
What do you need to pay attention to?
What practice could anchor you?

entries.passageText: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
entries.reflection: Jesus says the Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath. Rhythms of work and rest serve life. They are not burdens to carry.
studyPrompts: Is your life out of balance?
Do your routines serve you, or do you serve them?
What would healthier balance look like?

entries.passageText: and that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, even as we instructed you,
entries.reflection: Paul tells the Thessalonians to make it their ambition to lead a quiet life, mind their own affairs and work with their hands. Ambition can be for faithfulness, not fame.
studyPrompts: What are your ambitions?
How would a quiet life fit with them?
What does faithful ambition look like?

entries.passageText: But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
entries.reflection: Paul says the Lord is faithful and will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one. Protection comes from God's faithfulness.
studyPrompts: What do you need protection from?
How have you experienced God's faithfulness?
Whom could you pray protection over?

entries.passageText: “Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
entries.reflection: At Jesus' birth the angels sang of peace on earth and goodwill toward people. Goodwill is God's announcement. We can echo it.
studyPrompts: Whom could you show goodwill today?
Where is peace needed?
How does this song shape how you see others?

entries.passageText: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
entries.reflection: Hebrews says to lay aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and to run with endurance. Some things must be put down to run well.
studyPrompts: What weight are you carrying?
What would laying it aside look like?
What race are you running?

entries.passageText: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
entries.reflection: Jesus says he came so that we may have life, and have it abundantly. Life is a gift, and he wants it to be full. Your life matters.
studyPrompts: What makes you feel most alive?
What would abundant life look like for you?
Who reminds you that your life matters?

entries.passageText: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
entries.reflection: Jesus was born away from his parents' home town, laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn. The first Christmas happened far from home. God is present in improvised places.
studyPrompts: What holidays are hardest to spend away?
How could you mark them where you are?
How does Jesus' birth speak to being away?

entries.passageText: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
entries.reflection: The psalmist says God will show him the path of life, with fullness of joy in his presence. In transitions the next path is not always clear. Trust that it will be shown.
studyPrompts: What transition are you facing?
What path are you looking for?
Where do you find joy in God's presence?

entries.passageText: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”
entries.reflection: Jesus says that where two or three are gathered in his name, he is there among them. Faith is not meant to be lived alone. Even a small gathering is enough.
studyPrompts: Who do you gather with?
How could you gather with others in faith?
What does it mean that Jesus is among you?
